_what_this_is: Deliberate defects injected into REAL source on a throwaway copy. Each must make
the gate go red. One that escapes is a class of bug that can currently merge with
THIS FILE IS PROTECTED. A builder that can edit its own defect set can pass it.
_how_to_write_one: id      a name that says what broke, not which line changed
file    path relative to the repo root
find    an exact snippet from that file. Keep it SHORT and distinctive - a long
anchor breaks the moment anyone reformats, and a broken anchor is reported
as NOT_INJECTED rather than silently passing
replace what to put there instead
why     what it would mean if this escaped. You write this before you know whether
it does, and it is the sentence you will read when it escapes
_start_here: Six or seven is a real set. Aim at the seams, not at syntax:
- an invariant inverted        (a comparison flipped)
- a counter that stops moving  (the value exists, never changes)
- an output made constant      (always the same answer)
- an error path that succeeds  (the guard returns instead of raising)
- a persistence write dropped  (works until a restart)
- an off-by-one at a boundary  (right on average, wrong at the edge)
If the product has a screen, add these three. Every archetype above is
logic-shaped, so a set built only from them never exercises the rungs a
browser exists for - and all three below are one-line find/replace edits
in CSS or a template, which the runner handles the same as any other:
- a colour that stops tracking state  (the class is set, the value is fixed)
- an element that stays visible       (the hide is removed; the data is still right)
- a computed dimension pinned         (a width/position hardcoded, not derived)
AIM AT LEAST ONE DEFECT AT EACH RUNG, and read which rung caught each one.
ci.py stops at the first red rung, so a set built only from logic defects gets
caught entirely by 'unit' - and the e2e, holdout and gate rungs are never once
shown to be able to fail. A real build scored 9/9 that way: the number read as
'the gate can fail' when all it meant was 'the unit suite can fail'. The runner
prints the catching rung per defect. If every line says 'by unit', it is not a
finished set - add one that only an end-to-end assertion would notice, and one
that only the holdout would.

_lesson: The FIRST version of this defect was a no-op. It referenced a local that does
not exist yet at that point in the function, so the expression evaluated to 0
and the hash was unchanged - the defect injected perfectly and changed nothing,
and was reported as CAUGHT because the gate went red for an unrelated reason.
A defect you have not watched change behaviour is a defect that proves nothing.
Prefer the simplest possible mutation with an obvious effect.
defects.why: idempotence is a hard invariant; if this escapes, the same URL silently yields two codes and nothing notices
a counter that exists and never moves - the shape of defect an assertion that only checks presence cannot see
everything works until a restart; only a scenario that crosses a process boundary catches it

defects.find: raise ValueError("url must be http or https")
defects.why: an error path that silently succeeds instead of raising - a security invariant turned into a coercion
the unhappy path stops being unhappy; a suite that only tests the happy path never notices
an output made constant. The endpoint answers, the shape is right, the number is a lie
